home.title: A language for agents.
home.tagline: Writing code is only the beginning.
home.description: zxc is a programming language and compiler for AI agents. It gives generated programs a structure that people and other agents can come back to, understand, and change.
home.rxDescription: RX describes how work connects. Its XML names the calls and the values moving between them, so you can read the shape of a workflow before opening every function.
home.zxDescription: ZX holds the calculation itself. It looks familiar if you know TypeScript, with a smaller set of constructs and concrete types the compiler can check.
home.howItWorks: From source to a running program
home.howDescription: The compiler checks ZX, turns it into a typed representation, and generates Zig. It catches things such as mismatched types, reused values that have been consumed, and circular imports.
home.hostDescription: Your host runs the generated code and provides memory, I/O, and state. That boundary stays visible: compiling a calculation and running an application are separate steps.
home.aboutDescription: zxc is an experimental project by MATRIXAGES, developed in the open. ZX compiles to Zig today; RX validates module structure and dependencies. An RX execution runtime and database are not yet implemented.
home.whyDescription: An agent can write another function quickly. A few changes later, it can be hard to tell where a rule lives, what depends on it, or who owns the data. The next task begins with the same detective work.
home.whyApproach: We want each edit to fit the program around it. zxc gives responsibilities a place to live and makes the connections between them visible in the code. Some of those decisions become compiler rules, so they survive beyond the prompt that introduced them.
home.useTitle: Give the work a place to live
home.useIntro: A price calculation, an eligibility rule, a data transformation: each can be a small ZX function with a defined input and result. RX connects those pieces into a larger workflow. You can change how a price is calculated without burying that decision inside the code that coordinates an order.
home.agentTitle: Something the next agent can pick up
home.agentDescription: An agent rarely starts with the whole story. It may be joining an existing project, returning after a long pause, or repairing someone else’s change. A named module and a clear input and output give it somewhere concrete to begin.
home.agentContext: That is the advantage we are working toward: less architecture to reconstruct before the next edit. The compiler provides feedback on mistakes it can detect; the shared guides explain how to work with the rest. People can follow the same structure when reviewing what changed.
home.returnTitle: Code you can come back to
home.returnDescription: A discount now applies only above a certain amount. You want to find the calculation, see what calls it, and check the boundary. Answering those questions should not require retracing an entire conversation with an agent.
home.returnReview: This is the kind of work we have in mind for zxc. Keep the calculation small, give its inputs names, and leave the connections visible. When someone opens the project next month, the code should still explain the decision well enough to change it.
home.judgementTitle: There is still a person in the loop
home.judgementDescription: A compiler can reject a mismatched type. It cannot tell you whether a discount is fair or whether a policy matches your promise to a customer.
home.judgementReview: You bring the examples that matter and decide what good behavior looks like. The agent writes the change; you need a program you can question.
home.aboutInvitation: The language is still taking shape. If you try it, we would like to hear where you had to guess, where a diagnostic left you stuck, or where a small change became a large one. A concrete example is a useful place to begin.
home.principle: The next change should not need the whole story.
home.boundaryZx: Typed calculations. Checked, then compiled to Zig.
home.boundaryRx: Workflow structure. Module and dependency checks; execution is still ahead.
home.boundaryYouDetail: The rule itself, the examples, and the decision to ship.
home.changeCaption: One rule changes. The surrounding workflow stays readable.
home.changeNote: Function-body excerpt. The input adds minimum: u64; the caller guarantees discount ≤ amount.

copy.prompt: Use zxc for this task. Read {url} first. Confirm the available compiler and host runtime capabilities. Separate RX orchestration from ZX logic, keep dependencies acyclic, and report only checks you actually ran. Ask for the business goal and expected inputs and outputs if they are missing.

agent.intro: Read capabilities before generating code. RX orchestration and ZX computation have different implementation boundaries. Links are relative to this origin.
